title.rendered: The Art and Thought of Climate Change

content.rendered:
This global online event launches a special issue of Philosophy Today (70.1) on climate change, edited by Pratt Institute’s Travis Holloway. The issue’s thirty-two essays, interviews, and book reviews describe the conditions of a new era of climate change and invite us to assemble as friends of all the living.

Topics include contemporary climate art and aesthetics, trans and queer ecology, decolonial theory, climate history, political theory, climate philosophy, comparative philosophy, and the ethics of emerging technologies such as AI. Contributors include Dipesh Chakrabarty, Mohamed Amer Meziane, Timothy Morton, the We Smell Gas collective, Aimee van Wynsberghe, Yuk Hui, Hiroshi Abe, Thomas Khurana, Thomas Nail, María Cariola, Leela Gandhi, Perry Zurn, Claudia Baracchi, Lynne Huffer, and others.

The event will be co-moderated by Andrés Saenz de Sicilia of The Philosopher and Travis Holloway, editor of the special issue and author of How to Live at the End of the World.

title.rendered: Evidence of Transformative Sustainability Outcomes in Pratt Shows

content.rendered:
Part of Pratt Earth Action Week (Nov 2–7), presented by the Pratt Sustainability Center.

Does Pratt Shows Design student work suggest that Pratt’s sustainability education is transformative? Find out!

As sustainability educators, we don’t just want students to understand sustainability concepts, we want sustainability values to be manifested in their actions. We use a four-year analysis of undergraduate work from Pratt Shows Design to better understand the impact that sustainability education has on the creation of their thesis work. We also look at transformative learning outcomes beyond sustainability, comparing how the prevalence of other prosocial values compares to sustainability.

With Chris Jensen (Professor, Math & Science), Ashley Bales (Associate Professor, Math & Science), and Dan Boscov-Ellen (Assistant Professor, Social Science & Cultural Studies).

This event is scheduled as part of the School of Liberal Arts and Sciences’ “Works in Progress” series.

title.rendered: Growing Together: Creative Workshops for Local Ecologies

content.rendered:
A creative workshop exploring community, place and our relationship with living systems.

Growing Together is a participatory online workshop exploring how creative practice can support the exchange of knowledge around local materials and ecologies. Through examples of living materials, site responsive workshops and fieldwork methods, the session looks at how engaging directly with an environment can shape both creative practice and the way participatory work is developed with communities.

Participants will carry out a short fieldwork exercise in their own surroundings, using their observations to identify a local material or ecological condition as the basis for a simple workshop proposal. “Growing Together” asks how local conditions can shape not only what we make, but how knowledge is gathered and shared through participatory practice.

The session is intended for students and practitioners working across design, art, education and environmental practice. No specialist materials or prior experience are required.

Speaker:

Charlie Butterfield – Instagram: @charliebee.cosmology)

This event is part of Pratt Earth Action Week, Fall 2026 (November 2-7).

title.rendered: Nature as Inspiration: Bio-Inspired Student Projects

content.rendered:
What can we learn from nature? Explore first-year students’ inventive, bio-inspired projects in art, animation, and sustainable design.

This digital presentation features a selection of first-year Foundation students’ self-directed, bio-inspired design projects in a variety of media. Each project explores an animal or organic form through research, biomimicry, sustainable design, and creative expression, inviting curiosity about the natural world. From sharks and peacocks to the mantis shrimp, students translate nature’s forms and strategies into imaginative work, including zines, paintings, animated videos, and design prototypes. The presentation will be hosted on Milanote, allowing viewers to explore the students’ projects, research, and creative processes online. View it any time during Pratt Earth Action Week.

Presenters:

Carol Diamond, Adjunct Professor, CCE, Foundation
Yi Xin Tong, Assistant Professor, Foundation, Departmental Sustainability Coordinator

This event is part of Pratt Earth Action Week, Fall 2026 (November 2-7).

title.rendered: Sustainability for Every Body: The Future of Fashion Is Size Inclusive

content.rendered:
Sizing that ignores most bodies drives overproduction, returns, and waste. Original research, action steps, and Q&A. In person.

About 70% of US women wear plus sizes, yet many brands stop designing near a 34-inch waist. Mallorie Dunn, founder of SmartGlamour and Pratt Visiting Faculty, shares original body measurement research and shows how misfit drives overproduction, returns, and waste. Attendees leave with action steps for consumers, designers, and policymakers. In person. For the people making the clothes, and anyone who wears them. Expect frank discussion of body size and time for Q&A.

Speaker:
Mallorie Dunn – Visiting Faculty, Fashion Design; Owner/Designer of SmartGlamour (@smart_glamour)

title.rendered: PALS Present: Fall 2026 Showcase

content.rendered:
The Partnership for Academic Leadership in Sustainability (PALS) promotes academic sustainability in art and design higher education institutions. We believe it’s vital that creative education places sustainability at its core, preparing artists and designers to lead in shaping a more sustainable future.

​PALS PRESENTS

​This is a new, semi-annual virtual event, showcasing the work of our PALS partners throughout the year.
Faculty and academic staff working on sustainability in art & design higher ed will share their work and experiences.
Come to connect, gain inspiration, and get excited for the PALS Summit in March 2027.

​​Fall Showcase Presenters:

​Christine Facella (Parsons School of Design) – Warm, Fuzzy, Toxic – Adventures with Milkweed Fiber
​David Bergman (Parsons School of Design) – Future Visioning as a Path to Creative Thinking in Sustainability
​Gweny Jin (Columbus College of Art and Design) – Edge Condition: Teaching Design for a New Frontline Between Human and Nature
​Hannes Charen and Harriet Harriss (Pratt Institute) – Critical Death Studies Cross-disciplinary Program
​Lauren Simmons (Milwaukee Institute of Art and Design) – Mycelial Networking in Art & Design: Guided Conversation & Exploration of Sustainable Approaches
​Melanie McClintock (College for Creative Studies) – FlowState: Ephemeral Matter, Living Finishes, and Circular Futures
​Nicole Hall (School of the Art Institute of Chicago) – The Living Archive: Teaching Sustainability Through Memory, Material, and Landscape
Shelley Danner and Ian Lambert (College for Creative Studies) – Elevating Sustainability Practices Through Community Arts

title.rendered: Pratt Public Sphere Geodesic Dome Build-Up

content.rendered:
Build a geodesic dome and explore sustainable design, ecological experimentation, and community resilience through hands-on collaboration.

Join us for a hands-on geodesic dome build-up at the Pratt Public Sphere, a living laboratory for sustainability, climate justice, and community resilience at Pratt Institute.

Working collaboratively, participants will engage with the assembly of a geodesic dome while exploring sustainable design, low-impact construction, and the relationship between the built environment and ecological systems. The activity offers an opportunity to learn through making, exchange ideas across disciplines, and consider how creative, community-centered spaces can support environmental awareness and resilience.

The Pratt Public Sphere brings together art, architecture, design, and environmental practice to explore practical responses to climate and social challenges. Through collective building and experimentation, this event invites participants to experience sustainability as something we can actively create together.

Location:
Drop in any time between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM. Held outdoors in the Pratt Rose Garden, weather permitting.

Hosted by:
Rafael de Balanzo Joue – Professor, Pratt Institute (instagram.com/rafaeldebalanzo); Connor Campbell, School of Architecture student, 3rd year

This event is part of Pratt Earth Action Week, Fall 2026 (November 2-7).

title.rendered: Climate and Political Storylines for the Future

content.rendered:
Scenario planning for alternative climate futures: what science, policy, economic, design, and societal changes are needed?

Re-inventing the future: a storylines scenario-building workshop to help ideate on and center different climate futures. What are the science, political, economic, and societal changes and tools we need to achieve different climate futures? Are there existing tools and technologies, or are there things we’ve never created that have to be invented? The IPCC uses five core storylines to illustrate different climate outcomes and assess wider socio-economic impacts. The workshop will start from there and invite attendees to explore alternate scenarios and build their own climate futures in groups.

Facilitator:
Martha Molfetas – Visiting Assistant Professor, Graduate Center for Planning and the Environment

This event is part of Pratt Earth Action Week, Fall 2026 (November 2-7).

title.rendered: ARBORETA Sound Collective: Biosonification Sound Bath

content.rendered:
A stress-reducing sound bath using flute, cello, singing bowls, and biosonified plant sounds. Sit, lie down, or move as you listen.

ARBORETA is a socially engaged sound collective that offers participatory sound baths with the community it serves.

The founding members are composed of Creative Arts Therapy candidate Sal Daña (they/them) and Grammy winning cellist Leah Coloff (she/they).

The practitioners use flute, cello, and singing bowls to provide an acoustic soundscape that attunes to the parasympathetic nervous system, reducing stress levels in listening participants.

This sound session will include the use of biosonification to incorporate the sounds from a plant.

Participants are free to sit, lay, or move to absorb the sound bath.

The group has an ongoing collaboration with the Resilience, Wellness, and Well-being Center at Pratt.

Presenters:
Sal Daña – Creative Arts Therapy
Sam Harvey – Resilience, Wellness, and Well-being Center

Location:
East Hall 303 | Pratt Wellness Center

title.rendered: Sustainable Mediums in Painting, Part 1: Egg Tempera & Watercolor

content.rendered:
Make your own paint using sustainable binders like egg yolk and gum arabic, with less-toxic pigments.

Come make your own paint using sustainable binders such as egg yolk and gum arabic (egg tempera and watercolor). We’ll supply the materials and formulas so you can replicate these paint-making recipes, explain why these materials are more sustainable (they’re bound with natural materials instead of petroleum derivatives, and use less-toxic pigments), demonstrate how to make the paints, and have you make some of your own.


Location:
Pratt Institute | South Hall – basement room 001

Facilitators:
Estefania Velez Rodriguez – Adjunct Associate Professor, Fine Arts
Cathy LeCleire Wright – Full Time CCE Adjunct Professor, Fine Arts

This event is part of Pratt Earth Action Week, Fall 2026 (November 2-7).

title.rendered: Writing a Living Land Acknowledgment Session 2

content.rendered:
The Pratt Institute Living Land Acknowledgement is the only official document generated by the Institute containing principles with respect to Indigenous knowledges. It is an aspirational document that seeks to not only acknowledge the significance of Indigenous creativity but to “actively work to challenge the legacy of settler colonialism, undo its extractive and exploitative land practices, and express gratitude to the stewards of the land and water who came before us, and honor their descendants who are here today.”

In session 2, participants will spend some time drafting their own living land acknowledgments—drawing on their reflective thinking and writing from the first session—as well as discussing what makes an effective living land acknowledgement and providing feedback to one another. We will conclude by discussing next steps for writing. Facilitated by Emily Martin (Writing) and Dan Boscov Ellen (SSCS) and moderated by Jeffrey Hogrefe (HMS).

title.rendered: Supporting Faculty at Pratt: A Conversation with NCFDD

content.rendered:
Please join us for an afternoon of conversation and connection. Coffee and cookies will be served!

All faculty and staff interested in faculty development are welcome to attend.

Join us for a conversation with Frank Sesso, Partner Success Director of NCFDD, to explore the professional development resources available to Pratt faculty through the Institute’s NCFDD institutional membership.

NCFDD (formerly known as the National Center for Faculty Development & Diversity) offers a range of resources, through its online platform, designed to support faculty across career stages, including mentoring, professional development, writing and productivity strategies, career planning, and building supportive professional networks.

This informal gathering will provide an opportunity to learn more about NCFDD’s offerings, consider how these resources might complement faculty development efforts already underway at Pratt, and explore possibilities for strengthening faculty support across the Institute.

During the session, participants will have opportunities to:

  • Learn about NCFDD resources and how to access them through Pratt’s institutional membership.
  • Explore strategies for building networks of mentors, sponsors, and collaborators.
  • Consider how NCFDD’s offerings might complement existing faculty development opportunities at Pratt.
  • Share ideas about how these resources could support faculty across career stages and appointment types.

Please register using the RSVP button.

RSVP Here

We look forward to seeing you!

Hosted by the Office of Academic Affairs, as part of ongoing efforts to support faculty development across Pratt.
